title: Spanish greetings & introductions
examples: How do I say 'good morning' in Spanish?
What is the difference between tú and usted?
Can you teach me how to introduce myself?

explain.say: Today we are learning some helpful Spanish words.
If you meet someone in the morning you say buenos días.
To say your name you say me llamo followed by your name.
To ask how someone is you can ask ¿cómo estás? to a friend.
When speaking to an adult or someone you do not know you use usted.
Imagine you meet a new teacher in the morning you say buenos días.

faq.q: What do I say if it is afternoon?
faq.a: For the afternoon you can use buenas tardes instead of buenos días. You might also ask if it is time to eat.
asks: What time of day is it?
Do I change the greeting in the afternoon?

faq.a: No you should use 'tú' only for people you know well. For strangers or elders you must use 'usted'.
asks: When is it okay to use tú?
Who should I use usted with?

faq.q: If I say me llamo John, does that mean I am John?
faq.a: Yes it means that you are introducing your name. You are telling people what your name is.
asks: How do I state my name?
What is the phrase for my name?

faq.q: Does ¿cómo estás? change if I use usted?
faq.a: Yes it changes a little bit. For usted you say ¿cómo está? It is a small change in the ending.
asks: What is the formal way to ask how are you?
How do I ask a sir how he is?

faq.q: What is the difference between hola and buenos días?
faq.a: Hola is a general hello anytime. Buenos días is specifically for the morning hours only.
asks: Is buenos días only for mornings?

facts: Hola is a common greeting used all day.
Buenos días is used specifically in the morning.
Me llamo means 'my name is' in Spanish.
Tú is used for informal situations.

quiz.say: If you meet a friend in the morning, what do you say?
quiz.why: Buenos días is the correct phrase for greeting someone in the morning.

wrong.1: Hola is too general and does not mention the time of day.
wrong.2: Me llamo is used for stating your name, not for greeting.
wrong.3: This asks how someone is, not a simple greeting.

quiz.say: You are talking to your principal. Which form should you use?
quiz.why: The principal is an adult and someone you should show respect to using usted.

wrong.0: Hola is just a greeting, not a pronoun to choose from.
wrong.1: This is a time greeting, not a choice between two forms.
wrong.3: Tú is too informal for a principal.

quiz.say: A student says, 'Me llamo Alex.' What is the student doing?
quiz.why: The phrase me llamo directly translates to stating your name.

wrong.0: This phrase is used only for starting conversations.
wrong.2: Greeting is done with hola or buenos días.
wrong.3: Asking how you are uses ¿cómo estás?
